Google Wants To Make a 24/7 AI TV Channel. You’ll Be the Main Character

Google has filed for a patent that would use the information it knows about you to create an AI-generated TV channel full of personalized “shows” starring you and featuring customized advertisements. The patent is the latest signal of the AI video endgame: endless highly specific, customized content that is automatically generated based on the wealth of data companies and advertisers collect about you.

Tech companies regularly file for patents that they don’t end up actually putting into real products, but this one, called “creating a channel of video experiences tailored to a user,” describes a system that many AI companies have been clearly trying to build. It imagines something called “My Channel,” which would be filled with AI content generated based on demographic data, their video watch history (presumably from YouTube), and other information it knows about the user. It would then make “the user as the protagonist for the whole video.” The patent was first noticed by Patentlyze, a news site that tracks tech company patents, who shared it with 404 Media.

“You are a customized video generating model. Generate a customized video for a user where the user will play the protagonist,” a hypothetical LLM prompt in the patent reads. “The generated customized video includes characteristics based on the . The generated customized video follows the style and format of the of the user. The generated customized video sticks to the of the user but the narrative for the generated customized video is customized. The and parameters are ordered from more preferred to less preferred.”

It suggests that the channel would be connected to an “advertising server,” and that advertisements would be inserted into the customized AI content: “an advertising stitcher included in the advertising server generates an updated customized media content item by inserting at least one advertisement into the customized media content item,” it says.

The patent imagines, for example, “a crime/comedy caper,” “a fun romantic comedy,” “a sci-fi adventure,” and “an action/thriller experience” with a viewer named “John” as the protagonist. Another prompt included in the patent suggests that someone who had recently watched cricket highlights of a “Player 1” might then be served a similar video “that incorporates elements of the Cricket World Cup and Player 1’s recent performance. Perhaps [user_name] could be cheering for India in the stands or interacting with Player 1 in some way.”

The notable thing about this patent is that it is barely an evolution of what is already happening on social media and what is beginning to happen on streaming free TV channels on services like Samsung TV Plus and TCLtv+.

The people generating AI slop on social media are making incredibly specific content because they know that social media algorithms will be highly effective at filtering people there. Meta is already allowing advertisers to use AI to generate many slightly different versions of an advertisement; its targeting AI then automatically shows them to users who are most likely to react to a specific version of an ad. As I’ve previously reported, TCL has been experimenting with AI-generated content on its streaming free TV channels, and, even without AI-generated content, free streaming TV channels have gotten incredibly specific. It is now possible, for example, to watch reruns of individual shows 24/7/365.

AI boosters have long been saying the future of entertainment is allowing anyone to generate their own TV shows, or to generate “new” episodes of existing properties. An always-on, autogenerating, customized AI TV channel isn’t far off from that idea.

As I’ve previously argued, the future that tech companies envision is one in which we are somehow even more siloed than we are now. They imagine a world in which everyone lives in their own reality and watches their own, customized content, which is a world in which big, unifying pieces of media are harder to make and are few and far between. The Google patent comes on the heels of a Microsoft patent that describes a system that alters spoken words (and the person’s lips) in live video, thereby distorting reality.

University Approves Nuclear Weapons Data Center, Township Vows to Fight On: Last week, the University of Michigan’s board of regents approved the construction of a $1.25 billion data center that will power American nuclear weapons research. The regents voted 7 - 1 in a public meeting on November 19 to move forward with the project despite widespread opposition from faculty, staff, and the residents of Ypsilanti Township, Michigan where the data center will operate. A few hours after the vote, the leaders and citizens of the Township gathered to discuss how to stop it.

University of Michigan Mailer Promises Its Data Center Isn’t Really a Data Center: And, related, over the past month, the University of Michigan sent postcards and pamphlets to people in Michigan telling them its new data center is “NOT a commercial data center” and is, instead, a “research computing center.” According to one of the postcards viewed by 404 Media, the University’s data center will “advance breakthrough research in medicine, clean energy, cybersecurity, and engineering,” and "accelerate discoveries like new drug therapies and cancer treatments that improve people’s lives.” The University's postcard also promised to create 300 “high-quality union jobs during development” and “preserve approximately 80% of the 124-acre property as green space.”

The biggest story in the tech world is, once again, Nvidia and the Jensen Huang scandal. Outside of mentioning it in this newsletter, we haven’t really been covering this. The main reason is that these are one of the few types of stories that we’re not really set up to do. Nvidia is technically the most valuable company on the planet, and so other bigger news outlets have a bunch of reporters who are dedicated to covering just Nvidia. When a scandal like this breaks, they throw entire news teams at it. It just doesn’t really make sense for us to try to compete with our smaller team. The New York Times, Bloomberg, The Information, and the Wall Street Journal (and lots of other outlets) are all over this. It does feel bad to more or less sit out such a big news story, and it’s not that we don’t think this scandal is important. It’s just that we are usually trying to break new ground, and it’s hard to do that when hundreds of other reporters are laser focused on the same scandal. We reserve the right to jump in at any time, especially with a reported take or something like this. I do think it’s depressing that this has become a culture war thing, and an opportunity for Silicon Valley VCs and billionaires to do class solidarity and try to show that there should be no consequences whatsoever for bad behaving CEOs. I think the Trump and essentially stock market by blackmail aspect of it all is quite worrisome, too. Huang’s return raises all sorts of national security concerns, corruption concerns, and questions about how (much more) subservient Huang will be to Trump now that he’s done him a massive favor. I also found this exchange to be upsetting on many levels. Also, this post from Balaji, one of the worst to ever do it, is wildly deranged and will probably make your blood boil. Anyways, that’s enough of that for the moment. Here’s what else is going on.

In April, the Township’s utilities authority approved a moratorium on delivering water to data center projects while it studied how they might impact the community’s water supply. In response, sent a letter to the Township utility board threatening legal action.

Concerned Township residents have spent the past year strategizing with community leaders about how to delay or stop construction. The Township’s anger caught U of M off guard and it attempted to address community concerns in several public meetings. It hasn’t gone well.

The pamphlet attempted to contextualize the data center’s place in America’s nuclear weapons research. “It would not involve nuclear weapons manufacturing, physical weapons testing, or the storage of hazardous nuclear materials,” the pamphlet said. U of M did not return 404 Media’s request for comment.

On November 19, the board of regents approved the next phase of development for the data center in a vote of 7-1. 935af94a6ea6c2dc: LOS ANGELES: It was hijacked by the Penguin, careened through Gotham's streets and lived beneath Wayne Manor.
Now it can be yours — provided you have a Bruce Wayne-sized bank account.
The Batmobile — one of three custom-made versions used in Tim Burton's 1992 blockbuster Batman Returns — has gone up for auction in Gardena, near Los Angeles.
It serves as the centrepiece of a Julien's Auctions sale featuring dozens of pieces of Batman and superhero memorabilia.

With a pre-auction estimate of US$5 million (about RM22.3 million) to US$7 million (around RM31.2 million), the vehicle could smash the Batmobile auction record set in 2013, when the car driven by Adam West in the 1960s TV series sold for US$4.6 million (roughly RM20.5 million), including fees.

Known as the "Number One Hero car" and measuring roughly six metres long with two sweeping tail fins, the glossy black vehicle appeared in most of the film's driving sequences, Julien's noted on its website.
Since filming wrapped, the car has spent years on display at the Marconi Automotive Museum in Tustin, California.
It still features its original paintwork, engine and radio-controlled flaming exhaust system.
Julien's described the vehicle as "one of the most recognised and important cinematic vehicles in Hollywood history".
No matter who buys this Batmobile, don't expect to see it on the open road.
Julien's warned that the vehicle is "not street legal" and that its engine and transmission have only been tested a "limited number of times" since production ended.
The new owner must also follow strict rules set out in an agreement with Warner Bros. Consumer Products Inc., which manages DC Comics' intellectual property rights.
For example, the buyer must get permission before displaying the car at special events, and the vehicle "must remain stationary when exhibited to the public," the auction house said.

1e398f52c213f720: GEORGE TOWN: Penang is accelerating major water projects, including desalination and inter-state water supply, as demand is projected to rise by 27.2 per cent to 1,100 million litres per day (MLD) by 2032.

Penang Water Supply Corporation (PBAPP) chief executive officer Datuk K. Pathmanathan said demand stood at 865 MLD last year, with the projection based on feedback from the manufacturing sector, property developers and state development agencies.
He said Penang's limited land area and freshwater resources posed challenges to meeting future demand, particularly amid climate change.

"Penang occupies a land area of only 1,158 sq km. Looking ahead, we do not have sufficient in-state raw freshwater resources to support continuing rapid economic growth in the 2030s, let alone address the threat of climate change," he said in a statement.
The state's main raw water source, Sungai Muda, was also under pressure following increased water extraction by Kedah last year for its "5 Seasons in 2 Years Padi Cultivation Programme".

Pathmanathan said PBAPP had implemented several contingency measures since 2024 to protect consumers against disruptions to Sungai Muda and prevent the Air Itam and Teluk Bahang dams from running dry.

Under the Penang Water Supply Roadmap 2040, the Water Contingency Plan 2030 aims to increase treated water production by 602 MLD, build 4 water treatment plants in Seberang Perai and increase supply to the island.
The state also plans to purchase between 300 and 500 MLD of treated water from Perak under a project targeted for 2032, while exploring seawater desalination plants in the 2030s.
Pathmanathan said Penang's domestic water consumption averaged 267 litres per capita daily last year, 18.7 per cent above the national average.
He urged households to reduce usage to meet the state's target of 250 litres per capita daily this year.

0fc51390fa9c3aee: About half a million Californians were affected by the state's hike in minimum wage for fast-food workers. AP Photo/Jae C. HongEven before the 2026 midterm elections delivered a clear message about cost-of-living concerns, many states had been raising their minimum wage on their own as one way to increase workers’ purchasing power. And some have taken a more targeted approach, setting wage floors for specific industries. As the example of California shows, however, these initiatives can produce mixed results. In April 2024, California began requiring fast-food chains with at least 60 locations nationwide to pay a minimum wage of US$20 an hour, $4 above the statewide minimum at the time. The governor’s office estimated that more than 500,000 workers would be covered by this mandate. As a researcher of health and labor markets, I joined with economists David Neumark, Gary Wagner and Vitor Melo to run a study measuring the impact on California’s fast-food industry – specifically, whether restaurants employed fewer workers because of the ensuing higher labor costs. We found that the answer depends on which establishments you look at. For the state as a whole, the law didn’t affect employment in any statistically detectable way, we concluded. But smaller chains did take a hit, with employment falling by roughly 20%, while the number of locations dropped by about 10%. New openings fell by 17%-20%, and closures rose by 9%-21%. This employment decline comes almost entirely from fast-food chains ceasing to operate in California, rather than from staffing cuts at the locations that remain. The impact of minimum wage hikes holds importance far beyond the fast-food sector. Their proponents point to the fact that the federal minimum wage of $7.25 an hour has stayed unchanged since 2009 and argue that states and municipalities need to take action on their own. Los Angeles is phasing in a $30 wage for hotel and airport workers, while California’s healthcare workers just received another scheduled increase. Vermont lawmakers have proposed a $20 fast-food wage of their own. In addition, a total of 16 states will raise their minimum wages across the board on Jan. 1, 2027. With the federal minimum wage unchanged since 2009, many states and municipalities have raised the wage floor on their own, including for specific sectors. AP Photo/Andrew Harnik Smaller chains see an impact The question of whether and how minimum wages affect employment still provokes a vigorous debate among economists. In California’s case, some researchers have found that lifting the minimum wage caused small declines in employment compared with other states; others contend that the effect on jobs is essentially zero. More broadly, some researchers have found that minimum wage hikes cost jobs. But the time horizon matters, and effects tend to get larger in the long run. Our study didn’t try to settle that disagreement. Instead, we wanted to find out how employers did adjust, and whether large and small chains responded differently. What happens when higher minimum wages raise one sector’s costs and prices while its closest substitutes – such as sit-down restaurants – keep paying the lower statewide minimum wage? We relied on a database that recorded every business location in the country by name, along with the number of employed workers, each year. That let us directly identify the chains that were subject to California’s law, count each chains’ national footprint to apply the 60-location rule, and track outcomes from 2019 through 2025: total employment, employment at locations that stayed open, the number of locations, and openings and closures. We also compared California with other states and separately compared each chain’s California restaurants with the same chain’s restaurants elsewhere. Finally, we divided the covered chains into two groups: The 20 largest, which account for about 60% of covered jobs, and the 261 smaller ones. For the state as a whole, we found that employment at covered restaurants was basically unchanged, and employment at restaurants that stayed open didn’t change. Among the 20 largest chains, there was no detectable effect at all for any of the measures we tracked over this period. But the smaller chains tell a different story, recording substantial declines in employment, locations and openings, while closures rose. How to reconcile the flat statewide numbers with the sharp effects on smaller chains? The largest chains employ most of the workers affected by the new minimum wage rule, so the statewide total is dominated by them. And the reduced entry and higher exit among smaller chains may have eased competitive pressure on the largest ones. A final point: The biggest chains tend to be the most automated, relying more on equipment such as self-serve kiosks that can reduce the number of workers needed. That may help explain the muted employment response among these larger businesses. Taking the longer view First, we caution that the absence of a clear short-run effect on total employment doesn’t prove that the policy won’t cause bigger job losses over time as companies adapt to the new law. We also can’t answer what happened to the workers at the most affected restaurants or what happened to prices at those establishments, although other research suggests they rose by 3% to 4%. That said, the law was implemented barely 2½ years ago, and some of the larger effects that economists might expect – such as the closure of labor-intensive restaurants or fewer openings – are already apparent among smaller chains. Second, it’s important to remember that California’s fast-food minimum wage applies only to chains with 60 or more locations. So the smaller chains in that range likely lack the scale, automation and pricing power of the national brands and are most sensitive to the new wage floor. Indeed, the law appears to have shifted California’s fast-food market toward its largest chains, a pattern that other researchers documented in a similar study that looked at Germany’s national minimum wage. For the cities and states now weighing wage floors of their own, the California evidence isn’t a slam dunk either way. It shows that the costs, broadly speaking, fall first on the smaller chains covered by the law – but whether it meaningfully impacts the largest chains is unclear. Liam Sigaud is affiliated with the Paragon Health Institute, a not-for-profit health policy research organization.

387667a188a01814: Bringing a classic MacOS Finder to Linux is all very well, but there's no shortage of Linux desktops… however, bringing one to 9front is even more unexpected – and even more useful.

9/UX is a new project by Jeff "Progrium" Lindsay, who was one of the people behind Docker, Webhooks, and more. When you follow that link, and you should, pay close attention to what looks like a screenshot at the top. It is not an image. It's a real live executing instance of the OS, running inside your web browser, running on top of hyper9. (That is worth reading too – it's an impressive project in its own right.)
As its GitHub repository describes, 9/UX is a "Macintosh-inspired graphical environment for 9front."

"9/UX brings the classic Mac and A/UX desktop experience (a spatial desktop, a global menu bar, consistent controls and dialogs, icons, and resource-driven presentation) to 9front, built the Plan 9 way: rio and libdraw draw the screen, 9P exposes every application's UI state and commands as files, namespaces define the working environment, the plumber opens documents, and ndb holds human-editable metadata."

Lindsay introduced 9/UX earlier this month in a short X thread, saying he "made my own kind of A/UX but on Plan 9." In its creator's own words, "it's slop", but this is kind of interesting, original, creative bot-assisted coding that we enjoy looking at. At the end of last week, he returned to explain more:
"9/UX isn’t just a pretty Mac-style UI on Plan 9. It's filesystem inspectable. Shell scriptable. Even the Mac resource file format can be used through the filesystem."

Regular readers may have noticed that The Reg FOSS desk is fascinated by Plan 9 and its FOSS continuation 9front. We've written and presented at length about this remarkable OS, and tried to explain its FOSS continuation 9front several times. But even with the best will we can muster, its unique GUI is not an especially friendly or easy one. Its idiosyncratic UI was inspired by the late great Niklaus Wirth's unbelievably tiny Oberon OS, which we have written about before. It's cryptic, and that's being generous.

The research and development effort that led to Unix didn't stop when Unix 7th Edition escaped from the Bell Labs in 1981 and mutated into Unix System III. The industry enthusiastically adopted System III and later System V. A decade after 7th Edition Unix, Linux became a GPL version of something very like that traditional Unix, closely followed by the BSDs – and between them, they have very effectively distracted most of the FOSS world ever since. Even so, Research Unix lived on, saw 8th, 9th, and 10th editions, and then was replaced by Plan 9. In 1996, many of Plan 9's limitations were overcome by Inferno – whose revival as InferNode we covered this week.

We always vaguely thought that if 9front were to receive an improved GUI that was slightly more compliant with later GUI design standards, it might be with a version of the Inferno UI… But apparently not. A new, easier, and yet still simple, clean and attractive desktop for 9front is here, and it looks like classic MacOS from the era of Apple's 68030 Unix A/UX.

We do not think the chances are high that the 9front community will adopt this with enthusiasm. Even so, there is an AI programming manual for agents, and we've seen some interesting looking LLM-assisted 9front apps of late. Several can be found in the agent9 distribution, which includes LLM-assisted ports of C++, Python, and Rust, plus a version of DOSbox, and even a package manager called pac9.®

71292026fbd5343c: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is exploring amendments to existing laws to allow Malaysians to display their identity cards (ICs) digitally through the MyGOV application, says digital minister Gobind Singh Deo.

He said current legislation does not permit the digital display of identity cards, unlike driving licences issued by the road transport department (JPJ), which are already accessible through smartphones.

“Looking ahead, we are proposing a system that consolidates identity cards, passports, birth certificates and marriage certificates into a single application,” he said in the Dewan Rakyat when winding up the committee-stage debate on the ministry's 2027 budget.

Gobind said the matter was discussed at a meeting yesterday involving GovTech, MyGOV and MyDigital ID, following Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's directive to expand the digitalisation of government services.
He explained that MyDigital ID would serve as a digital identity verification platform, while MyGOV would function as a centralised gateway for accessing various government applications and services.

“The first phase involves consolidating existing applications into MyGOV. We will then proceed to the second phase, which includes integrating payment systems to enable transactions such as passport renewals to be done online,” he said.

On data centres, Gobind said their development could serve as a catalyst for expanding Malaysia's artificial intelligence (AI) economy by providing the computing capacity needed by startups and emerging industries.

To support this, the government is developing the National AI Compute Exchange (NACX), which will consolidate information on available computing capacity across data centres while coordinating demand from both domestic and international markets.

“By developing data centres, we are creating an ecosystem or hub with sufficient computing capacity that startups and emerging industries can utilise to access AI services and further strengthen their businesses,” he said.
Gobind also stressed that data centre development must not compromise the country's domestic electricity and water supplies.

He said the government was encouraging investors to secure their own energy and water sources, citing Google's US$15 billion (RM63 billion) investment, which includes provisions for its own energy and water supply, as an example.
“Regarding electricity supply, we need to invest in upgrading our infrastructure to ensure that we can meet the demand.
"We have already established an 85% tariff for data centres, requiring them to pay for the electricity capacity they request, regardless of whether they fully utilise it," he said.
Gobind said the proposed AI Governance Bill is expected to be tabled in the Dewan Rakyat in the first quarter of next year.
He said the draft had been completed and returned to the ministry for feedback before being submitted to the Cabinet for approval and formal drafting.
Meanwhile, the Dewan Rakyat approved the ministry's 2027 operating and development expenditure estimates, totalling RM1.362 billion, as part of the 2027 budget.

Zi Yu-Noraqilah have already tasted success this season, winning the Estonia International Challenge in January. However, their best result on the World Tour remains a runners-up finish at the Super 100 Baoji Masters in China in May.
With several big names absent from the Indian tournament, the Malaysians have a promising opportunity to mount a serious title challenge.
However, India's world No. 19 Treesa Jolly-Gayathri Gopichand remain their biggest obstacle, with the top seeds standing between the youngsters and a potential maiden World Tour crown.
A meeting between the two pairs could provide an exciting title showdown if Zi Yu-Noraqilah continue their impressive run.
880c4fae9675dd67: China has extended the suspension of selected export control measures on dual-use products shipped to the United States until January 27, 2027, in a move that could help ease trade tensions between the world’s two largest economies and provide greater supply chain certainty for American manufacturers. China’s Ministry of Commerce announced the extension on Tuesday, […]
58cbffe4a4c07471: PETALING JAYA: DAP will field Roderick Wong for the Meradong seat in the Dec 12 Sarawak state election.
In a Facebook post, Sarawak DAP chief Chong Chieng Jen said he signed Wong's letter of appointment as the party's candidate today.
"May he help bring another independent and courageous voice into the Sarawak state assembly. One that speaks for the people, rather than merely flattering those in power," said Chong.
Wong is DAP's 12th and final candidate for the Sarawak polls. In the 2021 state polls, DAP contested 26 seats but only managed to win two.
This time, the party has reached a pact with Parti Bansa Dayak Sarawak and will also avoid clashes with fellow Pakatan Harapan component PKR. Amanah has decided to skip the election.
Meradong has been under the Sarawak United Peoples' Party (SUPP), a Gabungan Parti Sarawak component, for decades but DAP held the seat for two terms from 2006 to 2016.
The state seat falls under the Sarikei parliamentary constituency, which DAP held from 2013 before SUPP regained it in 2022.
9e269318a29948f7: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is studying amendments to allow the MyKad to be accessed digitally, as existing laws do not permit the identity card to be issued in digital form.
Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said the ministry was also looking at integrating passports, birth and marriage certificates, and other personal documents into the MyGov Malaysia application.
He said discussions involving GovTech, MyGov and MyDigital ID were held yesterday following a directive from the Prime Minister.
"...we looked at ways to enable access to the identity card digitally," he said when winding up the debate on the 2027 Supply Bill at the committee stage for his ministry in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Gobind said users could currently view their MyKad details digitally, but not display the card itself, unlike driving licences issued by the Road Transport Department.

The ministry is integrating government service applications into MyDigital ID before moving them to MyGov Malaysia as a single platform for end-to-end digital services. The next phase will involve integrating payment systems to allow users to renew documents such as passports online.

Replying to Tan Kar Hing (PH-Gopeng), Gobind said the ministry was also exploring the use of artificial intelligence to speed up investigations by the Personal Data Protection Department, which has only 48 staff.

Under the proposed system, complaints would be submitted digitally, assigned case numbers and referred to investigating officers. AI would help identify potential offences and witnesses to be questioned.
b829a9bcf58cd4be: KUALA LUMPUR: Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang says the party is gaining support from non-Muslims who are uncomfortable with DAP, which he described as extreme.
He said Pas was confident of defeating Pakatan Harapan in the 16th General Election (GE16), citing the results of recent state elections.
"God willing, we can defeat PH. Look at the 2022 general election (GE15) results, as well as the results in Melaka, Negri Sembilan and Johor.
"These are good signs. It means even non-Muslims are no longer supporting DAP. They disagree with extremism, such as that practised by DAP," he told reporters at the Parliament today.
Hadi also pointed to the poor turnout of delegates at the Selangor DAP convention over the weekend.
On seat allocation between PN and BN for GE16, Hadi said it would be announced closer to the election.
Asked how seats would be distributed in the three Pas-led states, he said it was too early to comment.
"God willing, there will be no problem, whether it's a Pas or Umno candidate contesting. Wait for GE16," he said.
In the Melaka election on Nov 14, BN-PN won 24 of the 28 state seats, while Pakatan Harapan secured the remaining four, all through DAP.
At the Selangor DAP convention on Sunday, DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke warned that leaders who were absent risked losing their positions and said the party was in crisis mode.
8899018930a116cc: KOTA KINABALU: The Sabah government has been told to establish a special committee to oversee the proposed resettlement of Kampung Pondo residents on Gaya island off here.

Parti Solidariti Tanah Airku (Star) president Datuk Seri Jeffrey Kitingan said the proposed Pulau Gaya Resettlement and Residents' Welfare Committee should include representatives of the affected residents.

"I understand that most of the affected residents are Malaysian citizens. The government has a responsibility to them," he said in a statement, adding that the relocation could affect families' livelihoods, their children's education and their future.

On illegal immigration, Jeffrey said that his position remained firm, saying individuals found to be staying in Sabah unlawfully must be dealt with in accordance with the law, including repatriation where appropriate.
"Sabah must safeguard its authority over immigration matters. In carrying out that duty, the authorities must respect the human rights and dignity of every individual," he said.
Earlier, Star information chief Anuar Ghani had denied a viral image of the party endorsing issuance of identity cards to Kampung Pondo residents should Parti Warisan become the state government.
e91e6c51e5b397b8: KUALA LUMPUR: Privacy rarely survives the spotlight when you are one of the world's biggest pop stars, and now it appears not even virtual worlds are off-limits for The Weeknd.

The Canadian hitmaker—real name Abel Tesfaye—recently sent fans into a frenzy after posting screenshots on his alternative Instagram account, @gene.hackerman, showing a digital replica of his lavish Florida mansion inside Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6).

Situated along the coastline of Vice City, the in-game property bears an uncanny resemblance to Tesfaye's real-life Coral Gables estate near Miami, mirroring its layout, swimming pool, and waterfront position.
The singer purchased the sprawling peninsula residence in 2025 for roughly US$50 million (about RM206 million), according to the Malay Mail.

Surrounded by water on three sides, the real-world property features eight bedrooms, a private dock, and mooring space large enough for a superyacht—meaning millions of players can now virtually cruise right past his back garden.
Since GTA 6 launched on Nov 19, players have been combing through Rockstar's painstakingly detailed recreation of Miami and the fictional state of Leonida to spot real-world landmarks.
Uncovering an A-lister's multimillion-dollar home, however, takes digital sightseeing to an extravagant new level.
Adding to the coincidence, Tesfaye is already woven into the game's audio landscape.

His collaboration with French electronic duo Justice, "My Only Vice", is included on the official soundtrack, alongside his 2013 single "Wanderlust", which plays on the in-game radio station Flash FM.
7a1e2e9711be29d8: KUALA LUMPUR: Kerajaan sedang meneliti pindaan undang-undang bagi membolehkan kad pengenalan dipaparkan secara digital menerusi aplikasi MyGOV, kata Menteri Digital Gobind Singh Deo.

Beliau berkata, undang-undang sedia ada tidak membenarkan paparan kad pengenalan secara digital, berbeza dengan lesen memandu keluaran Jabatan Pengangkutan Jalan (JPJ) yang boleh diakses menerusi telefon pintar.

“Tetapi bergerak ke depan, saya memberikan cadangan bagaimana kita melihat kepada IC (kad pengenalan), pasport, sijil lahir dan surat nikah (perkahwinan) dalam satu aplikasi,” katanya ketika menggulung perbahasan Rang Undang-Undang (RUU) Perbekalan (Belanjawan) 2027 dan Usul Anggaran Perbelanjaan Pembangunan 2027 peringkat jawatankuasa bagi Kementerian Digital di Dewan Rakyat.

Gobind berkata, perkara itu dibincangkan dalam mesyuarat bersama GovTech, MyGOV dan MyDigital ID semalam, susulan arahan Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim supaya pendigitalan perkhidmatan kerajaan diperluas.
Katanya, MyDigital ID akan berfungsi sebagai platform pengesahan identiti, manakala MyGOV menjadi gerbang akses tunggal kepada pelbagai aplikasi dan perkhidmatan kerajaan.

“Fasa pertama adalah mengumpulkan aplikasi sedia ada ke dalam MyGOV, sebelum kita bergerak ke fasa kedua termasuk integrasi sistem pembayaran bagi membolehkan urusan seperti pembaharuan pasport dilakukan secara dalam talian,” katanya.

Mengenai pembangunan pusat data, Gobind berkata, kemudahan itu berpotensi menjadi pemangkin kepada pembangunan ekosistem ekonomi berasaskan kecerdasan buatan (AI) negara menerusi penyediaan kapasiti pengkomputeran yang mencukupi untuk dimanfaatkan oleh syarikat pemula niaga dan industri baharu.

Sehubungan dengan itu, kerajaan sedang membangunkan National AI Compute Exchange (NACX) bagi menghimpunkan maklumat mengenai kapasiti pengkomputeran yang tersedia di semua pusat data, selain menyelaraskan permintaan daripada pasaran domestik dan antarabangsa.

“Apabila kita ada pusat data, kita akan mempunyai satu ekosistem ataupun hab di mana kita ada kapasiti pengkomputeran yang mencukupi, yang dapat digunakan untuk syarikat pemula dan industri baru, di mana mereka sekarang boleh menggunakan perkhidmatan AI untuk memperkukuhkan lagi perniagaan mereka,” katanya.

Dalam pada itu, Gobind berkata, kerajaan akan memastikan pembangunan pusat data tidak menjejaskan bekalan elektrik dan air bagi kegunaan domestik dengan menggalakkan pelabur menyediakan bekalan tenaga dan air sendiri.
Beliau memberikan contoh pelaburan Google bernilai USD15 bilion (RM63 bilion) yang merangkumi penyediaan bekalan tenaga dan air.
“Untuk pembekalan tenaga elektrik, kita perlu membuat pelaburan bagi meningkatkan infrastruktur kita supaya boleh membekalkan tenaga yang diperlukan.

“Kita telah pun menetapkan tarif 85% ke atas pusat data di mana kita menyatakan bahawa walaupun mereka menggunakan atau tidak menggunakan bekalan tenaga seperti yang dipohon, namun mereka perlu membayar,” katanya.
Sementara itu, Gobind berkata, RUU Tadbir Urus AI dijangka dibentangkan di Dewan Rakyat pada suku pertama tahun depan.

Draf RUU itu, katanya, telah siap dan diserahkan semula kepada kementerian untuk mendapatkan maklum balas sebelum dibawa ke Jemaah Menteri bagi mendapatkan persetujuan dan memuktamadkan penyediaannya.
Dewan Rakyat kemudian meluluskan Anggaran Perbelanjaan Mengurus dan Pembangunan 2027 berjumlah RM1.362 bilion bagi Kementerian Digital menerusi undian suara selepas dibahaskan oleh 12 Ahli Parlimen.
60d494204f8352e3: KUALA LUMPUR: Environmental protection will remain a priority in rare earth mining, said Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup.
He described the mining guidelines as "very strict" and said all applicants must meet the same environmental standards.

"When the mining guidelines are published, it will be very clear that environmental considerations will be one of the ultimate factors that we take into account," he said at a joint press conference during the 11th Asean Ministerial Meeting on Minerals here today.
The assurance follows Malaysia's agreement on critical minerals with France, signed last week.

Arthur said the government would hold miners to the standards they could achieve with available technology, citing methods that allow rare earths to be extracted without clearing trees or leaving behind retention ponds.
He said Malaysia had published its export requirements before approving the supply of raw rare earth materials to France for research.
Under the agreement, France will share its rare earth processing technology with Malaysia.
Malaysia has maintained a moratorium on raw rare earth exports since Jan 1, 2024, to develop its domestic processing industry.

Guidelines issued earlier this month allow exports for research and development or processing, provided companies commit to developing processing facilities in Malaysia within three years of approval.
41dd0478086459da: KUALA LUMPUR: Greatech Technology Bhd's wholly owned subsidiary, Greatech Integration (M) Sdn Bhd, has entered into two separate sale and purchase agreements with Penfabric Sdn Bhd for the acquisition of two industrial complexes in Phase 3 Bayan Lepas Free Industrial Zone, Bayan Lepas, Penang for a total consideration of RM153 million.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said the acquisitions comprise the first industrial complex for RM63 million and the second for RM90 million.

Greatech Technology said the proposed acquisition represents a strategic investment by the group in acquiring industrial properties strategically located within the Bayan Lepas Free Industrial Zone, Penang, which is an established industrial hub.
"With customers' projected demand continuing to increase, the group anticipates that its currently planned production capacity may not be sufficient to fully meet demand in the near future.
"The proposed acquisition will allow the group to enhance its manufacturing capacity in line with anticipated customer requirements and expected returns," it said.
The proposed acquisition is not expected to have any material immediate effect on the group's earnings and earnings per share for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026, it added.
4a9953cbfbaaf438: JETOUR has assembled more than 10,000 vehicles in Malaysia since starting production in 2025, as the Chinese automaker begins exporting vehicles from the country.
Its first overseas shipment comprised the Jetour Dashing, marking the start of its export operations from Malaysia.
The company is targeting additional markets in Asia, South America and Africa in 2027, with estimated export volumes of about 7,000 vehicles next year.
The exports are expected to position Malaysia as a manufacturing and distribution base for Jetour's right-hand-drive markets.
Since starting local assembly in 2025, Jetour has introduced five locally assembled models – the Dashing, VT9, T1, T2 and T2 i-DM.
Apart from manufacturing, the company has established a local research and development (R&D) team as part of its broader Asia-Pacific operations.
Jetour Malaysia chief executive officer Fu Yong said Malaysia was important to the company's long-term development in the Asia-Pacific region.

"Malaysia is an important part of Jetour's long-term development in the Asia-Pacific region. We see strong value in building local expertise and capabilities here, particularly as the automotive industry continues to evolve.
"Having a presence across manufacturing and R&D allows us to develop a deeper understanding of regional market needs and strengthen the foundation for our continued growth," he said.
Jetour said Malaysia will continue to support its manufacturing, export and technical operations across the region.
fb7a1ad02384f987: Amazon said AI agents recently found and exploited a zero-day vulnerability with no human oversight beyond a simple instruction to get root access on an East Asian university server.

The agents were running on Cairn, an open source AI penetration-testing framework. The hackers, who provided prompts in simplified Chinese and configured the model to the Chinese Standard Time zone, gave the agents a list of IP addresses and the goal: “obtain shell access.” In short order, the agents discovered a zero-day in an open source medical imaging AI application running on one of the target servers. The agents then exploited the vulnerability and gained full control of the system.
“These findings show that agentic offensive operations are already happening, and defenders should prepare for the speed and persistence these tools enable,” Amazon said.
58b9a15232b11b01: PETALING JAYA: Tributes have poured in for national laureate A Samad Said, who died at the age of 91 this evening.
Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said he was deeply grieved by the news and recounted how one of Samad's most renowned works had impacted him.
"Through the novel 'Salina' (1961), Pak Samad brought us closer to the lives of those often marginalised, allowing us to share in their sorrows and champion their hopes.
"His love for the people will live on through his literary works, as well as his steadfast commitment to defending the Malay language and fighting for justice," he said in a Facebook post.
Education minister Fadhlina Sidek recalled how she would often borrow lines from his poetry piece "Tulus" to express her love and gratitude to mothers who had sacrificed much for their children.
"Today, I write to pay tribute to a life that gave us all such beautiful words. He helped us express feelings or leave messages that we sometimes struggle to convey.

"Pak Samad's passing is a huge loss to us all. I hope that his works will continue to be read and enjoyed by the younger generation. There is still much for us to learn from his writings and musings," she said.
Government spokesman Fahmi Fadzil echoed his PKR colleagues, saying Samad's voice, thoughts and struggles would live on in the works he produced.
Samad breathed his last at 6.10pm today while being treated for a lung infection at Hospital Kuala Lumpur.
Born on April 9, 1935, in Kampung Belimbing Dalam, Durian Tunggal, Melaka, Samad was widely regarded as one of the most influential personalities in modern Malay literary history.

PAS information chief Ahmad Fadhli Shaari said Malaysia had lost a giant in Malay literature, describing Samad as having given a voice to the Malaysian society's conscience through his words and courage.
"My condolences to the family. May they be granted the strength and patience to endure this loss," he said.
Opposition leader Hamzah Zainudin's Wawasan also expressed its condolences, saying Samad's literary and intellectual legacy would always be remembered.
"May God bless his soul, forgive him and place him among the righteous," said the party.
Separately, health minister Dzulkefly Ahmad lauded Samad for his role in civil society, particularly in championing justice and human values.
The Amanah vice-president added that he managed to visit Samad at Hospital Kuala Lumpur this evening before he breathed his last.
"Personally, I will always remember how he stood with us in civil society movements and in the national political landscape with Pakatan Harapan," he said.
0d04d3ec99ddc49a: KUALA LUMPUR: The RM600 million allocation to restore the Sultan Abdul Samad Building complex and Carcosa Seri Negara, which was previously questioned in Parliament, has taken on a different perspective following French President Emmanuel Macron's recent visit to Kuala Lumpur.

Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the public response to Macron's visit highlighted the value of investing in heritage conservation and preserving the capital's historical identity.
Recalling the parliamentary debate when Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim first announced the allocation, she said the spending had drawn criticism from lawmakers.

"I remember the painful discussion in Parliament when the prime minister first announced that he would spend RM600 million to restore the Sultan Abdul Samad Building. Everyone said, 'What a waste of money'.
"But today, people can see the completed projects. When the French President came, people could see the results. What a great way to spend RM600 million," she said.

Speaking at the Kuala Lumpur Festival 2027 announcement and partners' reception today, Yeoh said the decision to receive Macron at Dataran Merdeka, with the Sultan Abdul Samad Building as its backdrop, was deliberate.
"We could have taken them to any of our newer buildings and attractions, but we deliberately chose Sultan Abdul Samad for a purpose," she said.

She said the visit, which attracted widespread attention on social media, had also drawn attention to other parts of the capital, including Pasar Seni and Medan Pasar, rather than focusing solely on its modern buildings and developments.
Yeoh said Kuala Lumpur's growth should not come at the expense of its heritage, adding that historic landmarks must remain part of the city's identity as it continued to develop.
She said the government wanted younger generations to understand Kuala Lumpur's history, enjoy its public spaces and develop a sense of belonging to the city.
Restoring heritage buildings and bringing them back to life would also help make the capital a more attractive destination for international visitors, she added.
560d095b0ffc683f: KUALA LUMPUR: Sum Technology Bhd has secured a subcontract for a data centre project in Selangor with a provisional contract value of approximately RM48 million.

In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the company said its wholly owned subsidiary, Sum Technic Sdn Bhd, accepted the letter of award to provide mechanical, electrical, process utilities and firefighting subcontracting works.
"The details of the customer and ownership of the data centre have not been disclosed due to a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) signed between Sum Technic and the customer.
"The contract's commencement and completion dates have not been finalised at this stage," it said.
The contract is expected to contribute positively to the group's earnings and net assets per share for the financial years ending Dec 31, 2026, onwards until the project is completed.
2d0c6a548ffd0fb2: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is still considering an application to export rare earth carbonates to China, said Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup.
He said Malaysia had previously exported rare earth carbonates to China but that shipments had since stopped while some exports to the United States had been approved.
"We are still considering whether it will continue," he said when asked if exports to China would resume.
Arthur was speaking at a joint press conference with Asean Economic Community deputy secretary-general Satvinder Singh during the 11th Asean Ministerial Meeting on Minerals here today.

On Oct 27, the media reported DTEC Mineral and Metal Technology, a US majority-owned company, had secured a permit to export up to 700 tonnes of rare earth carbonate from Perak to the US for research.
It was the first approval under Malaysia's revised export rules, according to the company.
Malaysia has maintained a moratorium on exports of raw, unprocessed rare earth materials since Jan 1, 2024, to develop its domestic processing industry.
The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry said the moratorium would remain in force through 2027 and continue in the medium term thereafter.

Guidelines released earlier this month allow conditional exports for research and development or processing, provided companies commit to developing processing facilities in Malaysia within three years of export approval.
Asked about the influence of geopolitics on mineral investment, Satvinder said the bloc welcomed both Chinese and Western companies.
c18de82a91d2be46: PETALING JAYA: Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim berkata pentadbirannya telah meletakkan asas yang lebih kukuh bagi negara sepanjang empat tahun lalu, namun mengakui masih banyak yang perlu dilakukan untuk meningkatkan taraf kehidupan rakyat.

Dalam hantaran di Facebook sempena genap empat tahun beliau mengangkat sumpah sebagai perdana menteri Malaysia ke-10, Anwar berkata pentadbirannya berusaha memperkemaskan kedudukan kewangan negara, tatakelola diperbaiki, reformasi institusi digerakkan dan kebajikan rakyat terus diperkukuh.

Anwar berkata beliau memegang jawatan ketika negara berdepan pelbagai cabaran, termasuk ekonomi tertekan, kedudukan kewangan negara terbatas, peningkatan kos sara hidup, kelemahan tatakelola dan amalan rasuah yang sekian lama berakar.

"Sejak hari pertama melangkah masuk ke Perdana Putra, tekad saya adalah untuk memulihkan negara dan memperbaiki kehidupan rakyat. Bukan suatu perjalanan yang mudah, tetapi amanah ini mesti terus digalas dengan penuh kesungguhan.
"Perjalanan ini masih jauh dan banyak lagi yang sedang kita usahakan,” kata Presiden PKR itu.
Anwar berkata ukuran sebenar kemajuan negara adalah apabila kehidupan setiap keluarga menjadi lebih baik, rezeki lebih terjamin dan masa depan anak-anak lebih terbela.
Pengerusi Pakatan Harapan (PH) itu menambah bahawa beliau kekal komited untuk meringankan beban rakyat dan membuka lebih banyak ruang serta peluang yang adil untuk semua.

Anwar mengangkat sumpah sebagai perdana menteri pada 24 Nov 2022 selepas memperoleh sokongan Barisan Nasional, Gabungan Parti Sarawak, Gabungan Rakyat Sabah serta Ahli Parlimen daripada beberapa parti lain untuk membentuk kerajaan Persekutuan.
PRU 2022 menyaksikan Parlimen tergantung apabila tiada satu parti memperoleh sokongan majoriti untuk membentuk kerajaan secara bersendirian.

Dalam perkembangan berasingan, Setiausaha Agung PH Saifuddin Nasution Ismail berkata pentadbiran Anwar berpandukan empat keutamaan, iaitu kestabilan politik, kemakmuran ekonomi, kebajikan rakyat dan Tatakelola yang baik.

Saifuddin berkata memelihara kestabilan negara dan perpaduan rakyat penting agar agenda pembangunan dapat diteruskan, manakala manakala dasar ekonomi memberi tumpuan pada pengukuhan ekonomi, menarik pelaburan, membuka lebih banyak peluang pekerjaan dan meningkatkan daya saing negara.
Bagaimanapun, beliau mengakui masih terdapat kelemahan yang perlu diperbaiki dan beberapa harapan rakyat belum dapat dipenuhi.
"Kerajaan mesti terus mendengar teguran, memperbaiki kelemahan dan bekerja dengan lebih berkesan," katanya.

Saifuddin berkata baki tempoh pentadbiran kerajaan pimpinan PH mesti dimanfaatkan sepenuhnya untuk mempercepat pelaksanaan reformasi, memperkukuh ekonomi dan memastikan hasil pembangunan benar-benar dirasai rakyat
"Empat tahun kita membina asas. Dalam setahun berbaki, kita mesti bekerja lebih pantas agar rakyat segera merasai hasilnya. Keutamaan kita tetap rakyat dan masa depan Malaysia," katanya.
90f6befb325719a8: KUALA LUMPUR: The Special Jury Award received at the 35th Malaysia Film Festival (FFM35) was more than just an honour for Indonesian actress Aghniny Haque; it carried even greater significance because her talent was embraced and celebrated by the local creative community.
Aghniny, 29—who stars in the film Khadam—said she never expected to receive special recognition, especially as this was her first time taking part in the prestigious festival.
She added that the warmth and backing she received from fans and industry peers in Malaysia made her feel truly valued during her visit.
"I can't believe I've received this special honour. I am so happy and grateful to see how my friends in Malaysia have consistently supported and welcomed me."
"This is my first FFM, and it all feels surreal. All my hard work has truly paid off," she said in a Berita Harian report.
She added: "The greatest pride comes when one's work is well-received by the public. I am so grateful—I'm truly at a loss for words."

Beyond the festival, Aghniny hinted that she could soon appear in an action film produced by a local studio. "Yes, I have received a few offers, though things have had to be put on hold for now," she said.
Before winning, Aghniny noted that she had attended FFM35 primarily to rally behind Khadam, which earned 12 nominations.
Speaking about Melor, the character she plays in Khadam, Aghniny explained that this mute mother has a rare gift: conveying a wide range of emotions without uttering a single word.
She described Melor as a resilient woman who navigates life alone while raising her children in difficult circumstances.
"Melor is a truly remarkable person. She is a strong mother living alone, exhausted and overwhelmed by the constant worry of how to care for her children.
"Furthermore, she is mute and completely unable to speak. She also bears the heavy burden inherited from her own mother.
"Yet, even in such a situation, she remains steadfast in her commitment to look after her children. To me, that is extraordinary," she said.
Aghniny added that the award was a tribute to every mother working hard to raise her children despite the challenges life brings.
2c90c583b2ae6a81: THE third-generation Mazda CX-5 arrives with a bigger body, a more spacious cabin and a renewed focus on comfort.
But it is behind the wheel where the Japanese sport utility vehicle (SUV) has the opportunity to make its strongest impression.

Now in its third generation, the CX-5 retains the familiar Mazda emphasis on driver engagement while addressing some of the predecessor's practical shortcomings, particularly rear passenger accommodation and luggage capacity.

For Malaysian motorists who regularly travel between cities, navigate winding trunk roads or spend long hours on highways, these changes could make the latest model a more compelling family companion.
The new CX-5 is offered locally in a single 2.5G High variant, with a choice of a standard roof or a panoramic sunroof, and is fully imported from Japan.
Prices start at RM168,510, rising to RM171,510 for the panoramic sunroof version, before insurance.
More Muscle, Familiar Character
Under the bonnet is a naturally aspirated 2.5-litre Skyactiv-G four-cylinder petrol engine producing 185hp at 6,000rpm and 257Nm of torque at 4,000rpm.
Power is channelled to the front wheels through a six-speed automatic transmission.
While the Malaysian version does not receive the mild-hybrid powertrain offered in some other markets, the conventional petrol engine and automatic gearbox retain a familiar mechanical approach.
The output is adequate for everyday driving, although the CX-5 is not positioned as a performance SUV.
Its appeal lies more in delivering predictable power delivery and a balanced driving experience than in outright acceleration.

Mazda's G-Vectoring Control Plus system also works in the background to adjust engine torque and braking responses during cornering, helping the vehicle maintain stability and a more settled trajectory.
Finding Rhythm On Highways
On highways, the CX-5's larger dimensions and longer wheelbase should contribute to a more planted and composed driving character.
At 2,815mm, the wheelbase is 115mm longer than that of the outgoing generation, while the overall length has increased by the same amount to 4,690mm.
The additional footprint is particularly relevant during extended journeys, where a vehicle's ability to remain settled over changing road surfaces can make a difference to passenger comfort.
The naturally aspirated engine delivers its power progressively, rather than relying on a sudden surge of turbocharged torque.
Drivers looking for immediate acceleration may find the character less urgent, but the conventional six-speed automatic offers a familiar and straightforward response.
For highway overtaking, some planning is still necessary, particularly when carrying a full load of passengers and luggage.
The six-speed transmission can be operated manually through the gear selector, although paddle shifters are not provided.
Mazda Radar Cruise Control, with Cruising and Traffic Support, adds another layer of assistance during longer journeys.
It helps manage following distance and supports the driver in traffic, reducing some of the workload on congested expressways.
These systems remain driver aids rather than substitutes for attentive driving.
Trunk Roads Put Handling To The Test
The CX-5's more interesting proposition is how it balances comfort with driver involvement when the road becomes less predictable.
Malaysia's trunk roads often present a mixture of long sweeping bends, tighter corners, uneven surfaces and occasional changes in road elevation.
Such conditions place different demands on an SUV compared with the relatively predictable environment of an expressway.
Mazda has retained its driver-focused approach, with G-Vectoring Control Plus designed to make steering transitions feel more progressive and the vehicle more settled through corners.
The system works alongside the electronic stability control and suspension setup, rather than attempting to turn the CX-5 into a sports car.

Its front MacPherson strut and rear multi-link suspension arrangement is a conventional configuration for the segment, but one that gives Mazda room to balance handling response with everyday ride comfort.
The 19-inch wheels and 225/55 tyres also give the SUV a substantial road presence, although actual ride comfort over broken surfaces will depend on road conditions and tyre pressures.
On undulating routes, the longer wheelbase should help provide a more reassuring sense of stability, while the elevated driving position gives the driver a clearer view of surrounding traffic.
More Room For Family
Beyond the driving experience, the new CX-5 makes a significant improvement in practicality.
The longer wheelbase creates additional cabin space, particularly for rear passengers, while the wider and taller body gives the SUV a more substantial footprint.
Luggage capacity has increased to 583 litres, up from 442 litres in the previous generation.
That additional 141 litres is useful for families who regularly travel with several suitcases, shopping bags or recreational equipment.
The rear seats can also be folded in a 40:20:40 configuration, allowing longer items to be carried without sacrificing all rear passenger seating.
The wider rear door openings should also make entry and exit easier, particularly for families travelling with younger passengers.
Technology Takes Centre Stage
Inside, the biggest change is the redesigned dashboard, which adopts a more minimalist layout dominated by a 12.9-inch infotainment touchscreen.
The system supports wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, while a 10.25-inch digital instrument cluster and head-up display provide additional driving information.
A 12-speaker Bose sound system, wireless charger, ventilated powered front seats and dual-zone air-conditioning add to the cabin's comfort credentials.

The extensive i-Activsense safety package includes blind spot monitoring, lane departure warning, lane-keeping assistance, emergency lane keeping, driver monitoring and front and rear autonomous emergency braking.
Seven airbags and a 360-degree camera system are also included.
Putting family first
The third-generation CX-5 reflects Mazda's growing emphasis on making its SUVs more accommodating for family life, without losing the driving characteristics that have long defined the brand.

The larger cabin, improved rear passenger space and expanded 583-litre luggage compartment address practical needs that become increasingly important when travelling with family, particularly on longer highway journeys and weekend drives along Malaysia's trunk roads.
The additional safety and convenience technologies also reinforce this direction, giving drivers greater assistance while making journeys more comfortable for everyone on board.
At a starting price of RM168,510.40, the new CX-5 is not the most affordable option in its segment.
But Mazda's proposition goes beyond engine specifications and equipment lists.
It is about delivering an SUV that brings together driving enjoyment, everyday practicality and family comfort.

c15b0c1c356d78b4: WHENEVER the conversation turns to electric vehicle motorsport, the mind almost instinctively wanders toward multi-million-dollar spectacles: carbon-fibre Formula E single-seaters zipping around temporary city circuits, bespoke electric hypercars conquering global hillclimbs, or Le Mans-conquering hybrids that only the big manufacturers can afford to build and race.

To the average Malaysian independent garage owner or paddock mechanic, these high-end racing series feel like science fiction - impressive to watch on television, but entirely irrelevant to their daily livelihood.

Yet, these workshop owners are the ones who desperately need to upskill their talent if they want to remain relevant as the world goes electric, and there is no faster way to learn new skills than in motorsports.

If Malaysia is serious about upskilling its technical workforce for the electrified era, we need to start encouraging a new class of competitors: a separate hybrid class should be created for all levels of motorsport activities.
In fact, the government, through the Motorsports Association of Malaysia (MAM), must encourage hybrid class entries by setting aside prize money for organisers who are willing to go the extra mile.
With grassroots motorsports, we should focus on low-cost and accessible forms of racing - primarily Time Attack, Autocross, or Gymkhana.
The Right Discipline For The Job

Why Autocross? Because unlike high-speed circuit endurance racing, which places immense thermal strain on battery packs and requires massive cooling budgets, Autocross operates in short, intense bursts on closed tarmac lots or kart tracks.
A typical Autocross run lasts between 60 to 90 seconds.
It tests low-speed chassis balance, immediate torque delivery, regenerative braking calibration, and rapid thermal management under peak discharge cycles.
Crucially, it is also a discipline with a low barrier to entry.
The Motorsports Association of Malaysia regulations allow Autocross participation without requiring expensive full-welded roll cages, dedicated racing fuel systems, or specialised pit crews.
It is a sport where a street-legal car, a certified helmet, and a focused driver can compete safely and affordably.
Unlocking A Decade Of "Legacy" Hybrids
The second misconception about electrified motorsport is that it requires brand-new, six-figure battery electric vehicles.
Malaysia already possesses a vast, underutilised fleet of 10-15-year-old hybrid cars sitting in used car lots and independent workshops across the country.
First- and second-generation Honda Jazz Hybrids, Civic Hybrids, CR-Zs, and Toyota Prius or Prius C models are now accessible on the secondary market for modest sums.

Add to this existing pool the modern wave of affordable electrified offerings - from modern mild-hybrids to national entries like the Proton e.Mas series and Perodua's upcoming electrified platforms - and you have the making of a vibrant, multi-tiered grid.
For an independent garage, taking a decade-old hybrid or a modern budget EV and prepping it for an Autocross competition is the ultimate hands-on classroom.
To make an electrified car competitive in a timed slalom, a mechanic cannot simply bolt on an aftermarket exhaust or swap out a camshaft.
They are forced to engage directly with high-voltage battery cooling, inverter parameters, brake-by-wire feel, weight distribution, and energy recovery strategies.
Prize Money As A TVET Catalyst
Mechanics do not learn high-voltage diagnostics by reading government whitepapers or attending passive lectures.
They learn when there is a lap time to beat, a rival workshop in the next pit bay, and actual prize money on the line.
This is where public policy and agencies like the Ministry of Youth and Sports, MARii, or local automotive councils should step in.

Instead of sinking millions of ringgit into hosting foreign sanctioning bodies or high-end international race events that yield little trickle-down technical knowledge, a fraction of that budget could fund a national Electrified Autocross & Time Attack Championship.

By offering meaningful prize purses across distinct categories - such as Legacy Hybrid, Production PHEV, and Open EV - the government can create a direct financial incentive for independent workshops to participate.
To win, garage crews will naturally seek out high-voltage safety certifications, learn how to safely isolate traction batteries, reprogram power management units, and optimise thermal management.
Without realising it, racing converts neighborhood mechanics into certified, high-voltage-capable technicians - building the exact workforce required to service Malaysia's future electrified fleet.
From The Paddock To The Workshop Floor
The transition to electric and hybrid vehicles is often discussed in terms of charging infrastructure and showroom incentives.
But the long-term success of Malaysia's automotive sector rests on the hands that will maintain, repair, and engineer these vehicles once the warranty expires.
We do not need a glitzy, high-cost EV racing series to prove our technological credentials.

By embracing grassroots Autocross as an educational incubator, we can turn carparks and kart tracks into high-voltage laboratories - proving that the fastest way to upskill Malaysia's automotive workforce is through a set of cones, a stopwatch, and a checkered flag.

cea6858d5b9d2e2d: CrowdStrike has agreed to buy Zscaler for $43.9 billion in what would be the biggest cybersecurity acquisition on record, and customers are already bracing for pricier renewals.

The all-stock deal, announced on Monday, will see Zscaler shareholders receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for every share they own, representing a 34 percent premium on Friday's closing price. The transaction dwarfs even Google's $32 billion acquisition of cloud security upstart Wiz.

Buying Zscaler gives CrowdStrike a sizeable foothold in the network security market, where it will be going up against the likes of Palo Alto Networks and Fortinet. The plan is to combine Falcon's endpoint protection capabilities with Zscaler's zero-trust network security technology, giving customers a single platform for securing devices and the connections between them.

Naturally, there's an AI angle to the biggest cyber deal in history. CrowdStrike reckons owning both technologies will allow it to keep tabs on what AI agents are doing on corporate devices, where they're connecting, and what data they're getting their hands on.
CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz described the proposed combination as "cybersecurity’s operating system."

The acquisition also gives CrowdStrike's salespeople plenty to get excited about. Around 8,000 Zscaler customers don't currently buy CrowdStrike's wares, and the companies already have more than 2,000 customers in common. CrowdStrike reckons it can boost its annualized revenue by around $1 billion within 30 months of closing the deal by selling more products to the two companies' existing customers.

Some of those customers, however, don't sound particularly keen on being cross-sold to. Over on Reddit's r/sysadmin subreddit, news of the purchase was met with a familiar set of concerns from IT professionals who've lived through big-ticket enterprise software acquisitions before.
"As a zscaler customer, this does worry me. Cost increase, forced move to Falcon, integration issues, etc," wrote one sysadmin.
Another, whose organization already uses both vendors' products, added: "I think they're both great products but I imagine they'll jack up the price for our next renewal. Fun."

CrowdStrike intends to make Zscaler's products available through its Falcon Flex licensing scheme, which allows customers to commit to a certain level of spending and pick and choose the products they deploy. Monday's acquisition announcement didn't spell out what the deal would mean for customers who want to continue using Zscaler alongside a rival endpoint security product.

Others raised concerns about the fate of Red Canary, the managed detection and response specialist snapped up by Zscaler in August 2025. CrowdStrike already operates a competing service in Falcon Complete.

There may also be some nervous employees at both companies. CrowdStrike is targeting $500 million in annual cost savings within two years of completing the acquisition, identifying datacenter infrastructure, supplier spending, and wider operations as areas where it can trim the fat. Neither company disclosed whether that would involve job cuts.

Then there's the matter of putting more of the world's corporate security infrastructure in the hands of CrowdStrike, whose botched July 2024 software update took down an estimated 8.5 million Windows machines, grounding flights and disrupting hospitals, banks, and businesses worldwide. The incident gave IT departments a rather painful lesson in the risks of relying heavily on a single technology supplier.

The deal is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal 2028, assuming regulators and Zscaler shareholders give it the green light. Zscaler founder and CEO Jay Chaudhry will remain in charge of the business and take a seat on CrowdStrike's board.

CrowdStrike reckons the combined business will have more than $10 billion in annual recurring revenue when the deal closes. Judging by the reaction from some customers, they'll be keeping a particularly close eye on how much of that revenue comes from them. ®

c0f7df7687882154: LONDON: US stock futures and European shares came under pressure on Tuesday as the early euphoria following Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia faded, with investors cautious about further AI-driven gains and upcoming US inflation data.
Asian stocks jumped following a US stock market surge on Monday, when Nvidia's shares soared 31.5% after the AI chip giant reinstated Huang as CEO under pressure from US president Donald Trump.
The market bounce, however, failed to hold for a second day. Nasdaq futures dropped 0.9% after the tech-heavy index rallied nearly 7% a day earlier.
The pan-European STOXX 600 index dropped 0.1%, weighed down by a sharp drop in mining stocks.

Huang's comeback capped a whirlwind week of events that whipped markets and tore through the AI ecosystem, which has relied on Nvidia for everything from supplying chips to bankrolling the industry's massive buildout.
However, it also left unanswered questions over Huang, who had resigned following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged spy for China.
"With Jensen's return, it assures people massively and gives hope that the data centre construction continues and that boosts US GDP," said Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst, IG Group in London.

"But it then opens up a whole list of questions that may not be answered very quickly. What did he know? What else did he do? How much went to China? And these questions will continue to chip away at market confidence," Beauchamp said.
Nvidia's shares fell nearly 4% in US premarket trading, a day after marking their biggest daily percentage gain in 23 years and restoring nearly US$1 trillion in value to the company.
In Asia, Taiwanese shares shot up 9% from an eight-month low, with Nvidia's primary contract chip manufacturer TSMC and assembler Foxconn both nearly 10% higher at their daily limits.
MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan climbed nearly 4%, bouncing back from an eight-month low and recording its biggest single-day gain since July 31.

"By the end of the day, these businesses need to make enough money to justify investors' expectations. My point is: Jensen's return does not solve this. So, the sentiment is more emotional than sensible, in my opinion," Glenn Yin, director of research at online trading platform ACCM, told the Reuters Global Markets Forum.
Chinese shares were an exception to the relief rally, making only small gains due to concerns that tighter curbs on the exports of US chips are in the works.
Dollar, yields await inflation data
Investors are set to focus on Wednesday's PCE Index data, the last key data set ahead of the Federal Reserve's final meeting of 2026 in December.

New York Federal Reserve president John Williams said late on Monday that persistently high inflation continues to point the US central bank toward tighter monetary policy, while stressing that the pace of future interest-rate increases will depend on incoming economic data.

Fed funds futures traders are now pricing in a hike at the US central bank's December meeting as a certainty, compared with 89% odds on Friday, when stocks tumbled, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool. The market-implied chance of a supersised 50-basis-point increase is around 5%.
The US dollar index eased slightly from a 20-month high touched earlier in the session.
The sharp AI rebound has eased growth concerns and loosened financial conditions, reviving market bets for near-term Fed tightening.
The yield on the benchmark US 2-year Treasury note edged up for a second day and was last at 4.6684%, while the yield on the 10-year note edged lower to 4.9197%.
Brent crude futures dipped to US$88.75 a barrel, near a three-month low, on rising supplies from the Middle East.
Spot gold fell to US$3,619.70 per ounce. Copper, a key material used in data-centre infrastructure, retreated 3% after jumping 5% on Monday.

ce888dd41b16546b: PETALING JAYA: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim believes his administration has laid a stronger foundation for the country over the past four years, but acknowledges that much more needs to be done to improve the lives of Malaysians.

In a Facebook post marking four years since his swearing-in as Malaysia's 10th prime minister, Anwar said his administration had worked to strengthen the country’s finances, promote good governance, push institutional reforms and enhanced public welfare.
Anwar said he took office amid various challenges, including economic pressures, limited national finances, a rising cost of living, weak governance and entrenched corruption.

“From the first day I stepped into Perdana Putra, my determination was to restore the country and improve the lives of the people. It has not been an easy journey, but this responsibility must continue to be shouldered with full commitment.
"The journey is far from over and much more needs to be done,” the PKR president said.
Anwar said the true measure of the country’s progress was whether families enjoyed better lives, more secure livelihoods and their children had a brighter future.
The Pakatan Harapan chairman added that he remained committed to easing the people’s burden and creating more equitable opportunities for everyone.

Anwar was sworn in as prime minister on Nov 24, 2022, after obtaining the support of Barisan Nasional, Gabungan Parti Sarawak, Gabungan Rakyat Sabah and MPs from several other parties to form the federal government.
The 2022 general election had resulted in a hung Parliament with no single party commanding majority support to form the government on its own.

Separately, PH secretary-general Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said Anwar's administration had been guided by four priorities – political stability, economic prosperity, public welfare and good governance.

Saifuddin said political stability and national unity were necessary to ensure the government’s development agenda could continue, while economic policies focused on strengthening the economy, attracting investments, creating jobs and improving the country’s competitiveness.
Nonetheless, he acknowledged that weaknesses remained and some public expectations had yet to be met.
“The government must continue to listen to criticism, address its weaknesses and work more effectively,” he said.
Saifuddin said the remainder of the PH-led government's term must be spent accelerating reforms, strengthening the economy, and ensuring people felt the benefits of the country's development.
“Four years have been spent building the foundations. In the remaining year, we must work faster so that the people can feel the results sooner.
“Our priority remains the people and Malaysia's future,” he said.
611a0c001200fbd0: PUTRAJAYA: Badan Peguam berjaya dalam rayuan untuk dimasukkan sebagai defendan dalam saman seorang peguam yang memohon pengisytiharan bahawa Perlembagaan versi bahasa Melayu adalah teks yang sahih.
